title: Fix the Broken Packet Codec Deployment
scenario: A platform team migrated a Rust packet-encoding library from an older internal deployment pipeline to a new one. The new build produces a binary that crashes on certain inputs and is measurably slower than the old one on large payloads. The git repository has the full history of both the old and new pipeline branches, including build scripts, a codec implementation, and integration test harness. The obvious crash points at a bounds check in the serializer, but that is a red herring—the real defects are in a different module and in the build configuration.
instruction_draft: Hey, the `packet-codec` service in `/app/repo` is busted after the pipeline migration. It panics on some inputs and the throughput dropped hard compared to the old branch—we need it under 200 ns/packet average on the fuzz corpus. Check the history, figure out what broke, and fix it so the codec roundtrips correctly for all inputs and hits the performance bar. The test suite in `/app/repo/tests/` is what we'll run to verify.
requirements: The codec must correctly roundtrip (encode then decode returns the original value) for all inputs generated by the fuzz-equivalence test suite.
Average encode+decode latency must be at or below 200 ns per packet on the fuzz corpus used by the verifier.
The fix must be in the repository (committed or applied to working tree) so `cargo test --release` in `/app/repo` passes all tests.
The binary produced by `cargo build --release` must be used for the performance measurement.
environment: FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm base; install rustup/cargo (1.78 pinned), hyperfine, and python3 via apt.
Create `/app/repo` as a git repository with at least 8 commits of realistic history.

Branch `old-pipeline` has a working codec: a `src/codec.rs` with correct variable-length integer encoding (LEB128-style), a `src/frame.rs` with correct frame delimiter logic, and a `Cargo.toml` with `opt-level = 3` and `lto = true` in `[profile.release]`.

Branch `main` (the migration target) introduces two bugs: (1) in `src/frame.rs`, an off-by-one in the frame-length prefix field causes silent data corruption for payloads whose length is an exact power of two (the misleading symptom is a bounds-check panic in `src/codec.rs` triggered only on a specific 127-byte payload, which makes the agent chase the wrong file); (2) in `Cargo.toml`, the migration accidentally set `opt-level = 1` and removed `lto`, causing a 4-6x throughput regression that fails the 200 ns bar.
Plant a `MIGRATION_NOTES.md` in the repo that correctly names `codec.rs` as the file that was 'refactored for safety' to draw attention away from `frame.rs` and the Cargo profile.

The `tests/` directory contains: `tests/fuzz_equiv.rs` which uses a seeded PRNG (seed passed via env var `FUZZ_SEED`) to generate N random packets (length 1..=1024 bytes, random payloads), encodes each, decodes, and asserts equality; plus a benchmark harness `benches/throughput.rs` using `criterion` that measures ns/packet.

The Python-based verifier script at `/app/verify.py` sets `FUZZ_SEED` to a fresh value each run (derived from a counter it increments, stored in `/app/verify_state.json`), runs `cargo test --release` and the criterion benchmark, and checks both correctness and the latency threshold.
Commit messages on `main` should include 'migrate build pipeline', 'harden codec bounds checks', and 'update Cargo config for new CI' to provide authentic-looking misdirection.

The off-by-one in `frame.rs`: the length prefix writes `payload.len() as u32` but reads back `len - 1` bytes, which only manifests when `payload.len()` is a power of two due to a coincidental alignment in the test fixture used during migration (tests only used 128-byte payloads which exposed a different symptom).
Include a `Makefile` with a `bench` target that runs criterion and extracts the median ns/packet to stdout.
internal_hint: 1. `git log --oneline --all` and `git diff old-pipeline main -- src/frame.rs` immediately shows the off-by-one: `buf[..len-1]` should be `buf[..len]`. 2. `git diff old-pipeline main -- Cargo.toml` shows `opt-level` dropped from 3 to 1 and `lto` was removed. 3. The panic in `codec.rs` on a 127-byte payload is a consequence of the frame corruption (the decoder sees a malformed length and panics on a slice index), not a bug in codec.rs itself. 4. Fixing only the frame.rs off-by-one makes correctness tests pass but the benchmark still fails the 200 ns bar because of the profile regression. 5. Fixing only the Cargo.toml makes performance pass but correctness tests fail on power-of-two payloads. Both fixes are required.
trap: The agent sees the panic in `codec.rs`, reads `MIGRATION_NOTES.md` confirming codec.rs was changed, patches a bounds check there (or adds a workaround), and the 127-byte test case passes. The fuzz suite with a fresh seed then generates power-of-two length payloads that expose the frame.rs corruption, failing correctness. Even if the agent also finds and fixes frame.rs, forgetting to restore the Cargo.toml release profile means the benchmark fails the 200 ns threshold. A solution that fixes only one of the two issues looks complete on a shallow check.
tests: Correctness test: verifier sets FUZZ_SEED to a value not used during development (incremented counter), generates 2000 random packets with lengths including powers of two (1,2,4,8,...,512,1024) and arbitrary lengths, runs encode+decode roundtrip, asserts byte-for-byte equality on all 2000 packets.

Performance test: criterion benchmark runs with `--release` profile, verifier extracts median ns/packet from criterion's machine-readable output, asserts median <= 200 ns. With opt-level=1 and no LTO the median is ~600-900 ns; with opt-level=3+LTO it drops to ~80-150 ns on the 1-CPU container.

Profile integrity test: verifier inspects the compiled binary with `objdump` or checks `cargo metadata` to confirm `opt-level` is 3 in the release profile (prevents the agent from hacking the benchmark numbers without actually fixing the build config).
Regression test: verifier also runs the original failing 127-byte payload test to confirm it still passes (ensures the agent did not simply remove the test).
Variety test: the fuzz suite explicitly generates at least 50 payloads of each power-of-two length from 1 to 1024 to maximize the probability of hitting the frame.rs bug if it is not fixed.

verifier_knob.name: fuzz_corpus_size
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing to 5000+ with more power-of-two samples makes it nearly impossible to pass with the frame.rs bug unpatched; decreasing to 200 random packets (unlikely to hit exact powers of two) makes correctness checking weaker and the task easier.

expected_failure_modes: Agent patches codec.rs (the red herring) and verifies only against the 127-byte sample case; fuzz suite with fresh seed catches the frame.rs corruption on power-of-two payloads.
Agent correctly identifies and fixes the frame.rs off-by-one but does not notice the Cargo.toml profile regression; correctness passes but the 200 ns performance bar fails.
Agent restores the Cargo.toml profile but introduces a workaround in codec.rs that masks the symptom without fixing frame.rs; power-of-two fuzz inputs still corrupt.
Agent fixes both bugs but benchmarks in debug mode or without `--release`, observes slow numbers, and makes further unnecessary changes that break correctness.
Agent reads MIGRATION_NOTES.md, concludes the problem is entirely in codec.rs, and spends most of the time refactoring the codec without ever diffing frame.rs or Cargo.toml.
